structuredResult.summary: Proposed architecture: implement demo.LinkBook as one process-local in-memory domain object backed by a code-to-entry map. Each retained entry stores the immutable destination, optional expiration Instant, disabled/deleted lifecycle state, cumulative recorded-resolution count, and a map of UTC LocalDate buckets. Creation rejects any already-present code, so deletion changes state but never removes the reservation. Resolution performs eligibility checks before recording: missing, disabled, deleted, or now greater than or equal to expiresAt returns Optional.empty(); otherwise it returns the original destination and, only when record=true, increments the total and the UTC date derived from now. total and daily return zero for unknown codes, while retained entries preserve analytics after disable or delete. This is deliberately a domain-only fixture: no HTTP layer, persistence, destination fetch, external dependency, deployment, or reconstruction of the full service is proposed. The supplied pom.xml and acceptance tests remain unchanged. This architecture-only invocation wrote no files, did not implement source code, and does not claim that Maven verification passed.
risks: The current invocation cannot implement demo.LinkBook because narrative-only output is required and the sole allowed write path, artifacts/architecture/, excludes src/main/java/demo/LinkBook.java.

Actual verification remains outstanding. A later authorized implementation stage must run mvn verify against the combined candidate without modifying the supplied POM or acceptance tests and without weakening verification checks.

The contract does not specify null handling, behavior of disable/delete for unknown codes, or concurrency guarantees. The implementation should avoid advertising extra guarantees; any behavior needed beyond the supplied acceptance contract requires clarification or focused evidence.
All state and analytics are intentionally process-local and non-durable. This fixture must not be represented as the full REST/database service or a production analytics design.

Final human approval remains a separate mandatory gate after fresh implementation verification and candidate review; it has not been granted. Any recovery must retain prior failed evidence and obtain fresh design approval.

tasks.description: Record the proposed single-class in-memory design and its invariants: immutable destination, permanent code reservation, optional expiration with equality expired, retained lifecycle entries and counts, successful-recorded resolutions only, and UTC daily buckets.

After the control layer grants a separate owned source write path, create src/main/java/demo/LinkBook.java using the approved design while preserving pom.xml and src/test/java/demo/LinkBookTest.java exactly.
On the resulting combined candidate, perform a fresh mvn verify run and preserve the actual command result as verification evidence; do not alter the POM or tests to obtain a pass.
Review the verified candidate against every README behavior and the approved fixture boundary, preserving prior failed evidence and leaving final human approval as a separate control-layer gate.
